**Data releases and availability (2025–2026)**

The page has no announcements of formal Level 1, 2, or 3 public releases, and it doesn't mention quicklook availability by name. It does list these data-related items:

- **2025-03-14, "PUNCH LEOPS nearly complete; commissioning continues":** The spacecraft were "ready to transition to 'normal operations'" while commissioning continued on a single shift.
- **2025-03-24, "PUNCH SOC processes the first data":** The Science Operations Center received the first data packets, decompressed them, and reconstructed a test pattern image.
- **2025-04-13, "Dark frames are useful":** These "Level 0" (unprocessed) products were released with flight metadata. The post notes that Level 1 and higher remove detector offsets.
- **2025-04-17, "First light composite":** First-light images from NFI and WFI-2 were taken on 14 April.
- **2025-04-23, "A Polarimetric Rainbow":** A "preliminary data product" from WFI-2, described as uncalibrated Level 0 data.
- **2025-05-05, "NFI sees the new Moon":** The first full-orbit NFI science sequence ran on April 27 during commissioning.
- **2025-05-19, "PUNCH data are live online!":** "PUNCH images of space are now available for download from NASA's Solar Data Analysis Center (SDAC)." The data are in FITS format and updated twice daily from the SOC.
- **2025-06-13, "You've never seen space weather like this before!":** Described as a "preliminary movie."
- **2025-08-22, "Forecasting Shock-Associated Energetic Particle Intensities":** Refers to "QuickPUNCH image sequences" as an input to forecasting work.
- **2025-10-29, "The journey to 0.1% photometric calibration":** Describes the calibration work needed to merge images from four spacecraft.
- **2025-12-08, Outreach "first light" post:** The caption states the mission's "first light" was "released on June 3rd," which differs from the April first-light date in the 2025-04-17 post.
- **2026-03-11, "PUNCH celebrates one year of flight!":** The post says "We are still refining the data processing for the most complex ground pipeline produced for any Explorer mission."
- **2026-04-22, "A celestial staring contest":** Uses a "PUNCH intermediate-data-product movie."
- **2026-09-18, "A Year of the Solar Corona":** Version 0m, "in the process of being released," will be the first to include NFI photometric data in the mosaics. Versions 0a through 0l omitted NFI data.

**LOFAR2.0 status:** Hardware has been installed in all stations, and the Dutch array verification is still in progress. The newsletter says "As of October 1st, LOFAR2.0 hardware has been installed in all stations." About 25% of the array had been verified, and "The verification of the Dutch array is expected to be finalized by the end of the year." Commissioning is moving into science testing, with NL-scale imaging targeted for the end of 2025.

**When observations or science operations resume:** The newsletter gives no date for resuming Cycle observations. LOFAR1.0 production ended with Cycle 20 on 31 August 2024, and the newsletter says "Efforts are now being invested into completing the LOFAR2.0 telescope upgrade to start LOFAR2.0 production operations." It also notes that LTA support for LOFAR2.0 data products is "a pre-condition for the start of LOFAR2.0 science projects," and that large-program teams must submit Data Management Plans by 14 December.

**Solar, space weather, or IPS observations:** None are mentioned in this newsletter.

**LOFAR observing in Nov–Dec 2025:** The newsletter does not say. It describes commissioning activity around October 2025, such as imaging runs and tied-array pulsar observations, but it does not give a schedule for November or December.

Web search results for query: "Jian 2016 Space Weather "Validation for global solar wind prediction using Ulysses" ENLIL ambient parameters dfast tfast "a3b2" OR "a6b1" OR "a7b1""

Links: [{"title":"Unifying the Validation of Ambient Solar Wind Models","url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.13447"},{"title":"111 Jian et al 2016 Space Weather","url":"https://ips.ucsd.edu/ftp/pub/SCRPA_2019/111_Jian_et_al-2016-Space_Weather.pdf"},{"title":"ca78c760 8edd 48a4 8bd1 7891a3d63208","url":"https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/items/ca78c760-8edd-48a4-8bd1-7891a3d63208"},{"title":"pubid 312143","url":"https://vivo.colorado.edu/display/pubid_312143"},{"title":"pubid 312143","url":"https://vivo-cub.colorado.edu/display/pubid_312143"},{"title":"2 LanJian SolarScientistFeedback","url":"https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/publicData/workshops/2016/3_Wednesday_AM/2_LanJian_SolarScientistFeedback.pdf"},{"title":"13 Jian 201804 CCMC","url":"https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/publicData/workshops/2018/02_Tuesday_AM/13_Jian_201804_CCMC.pdf"},{"title":"jian ccmc2012","url":"https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/publicData/workshops/2012/Wednesday_pdf/jian_ccmc2012.pdf"},{"title":"Validation for solar wind prediction at Earth: Comparison of coronal and heliospheric models installed at the CCMC","url":"https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/items/0e5aba2b-1fb1-4f29-af41-6deae8aa233c"}]

The search found the paper and its publication details, but nothing that lists the specific ambient parameters (dfast, tfast, a3b2, a6b1, a7b1) you asked about.

- **Paper identity:** The paper is Jian et al. (2016), published in Space Weather vol. 14, issue 8, pp. 592–611 (DOI 10.1002/2016SW001435). It compares model results with Ulysses observations over seven Carrington rotations, covering several CCMC-installed coronal and heliospheric models. A full-text PDF is available from the UCSD IPS site (ips.ucsd.edu), which is the most likely place to find the parameter tables.
- **Parameter context:** A 2018 CCMC workshop slide deck by the same lead author notes that more than 10 parameters are used in setting the ambient wind conditions at ENLIL's inner boundary, and that these have been recently added in the WSA-Enlil result page as the control file. This suggests the named parameters belong to that control-file set, but the search did not confirm the individual names or meanings.

I did not find the parameter definitions, so for the specific names you need, check the full-text PDF or the CCMC WSA-Enlil control-file documentation.

Web search results for query: "Samara Arge Pinto 2024 "Calibrating the WSA model in EUHFORIA based on PSP observations" journal volume DOI"

Links: [{"title":"publi2-as.oma.be","url":"https://publi2-as.oma.be/record/7512"},{"title":"publi2-as.oma.be","url":"https://publi2-as.oma.be/record/7512?ln=en"},{"title":"The Astrophysical Journal (Jan 2024)","url":"https://doaj.org/article/d5d52bf50f7a4729a5203ae0dfc2fce6"},{"title":"publi2-as.oma.be","url":"https://publi2-as.oma.be/record/6509"},{"title":"EGU22-9583, updated on 10 Jan 2023","url":"https://meetingorganizer.copernicus.org/EGU22/EGU22-9583.html"},{"title":"Calibrating the WSA model in EUHFORIA based on PSP observations","url":"https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.09693"},{"title":"publi2-as.oma.be","url":"https://publi2-as.oma.be/record/6113"},{"title":"publi2-as.oma.be","url":"https://publi2-as.oma.be/record/6114"},{"title":"publi2-as.oma.be","url":"https://publi2-as.oma.be/record/6113?ln=en"},{"title":"Ref: CTALK-2023-0016","url":"https://publi2-as.oma.be/record/6114?ln=en"}]

The paper is **"Calibrating the WSA Model in EUHFORIA Based on Parker Solar Probe Observations"** by E. Samara, C. N. Arge, R. F. Pinto, J. Magdalenić, N. Wijsen, M. L. Stevens, L. Rodriguez, and S. Poedts, published in The Astrophysical Journal in 2024.

- **DOI:** 10.3847/1538-4357/ad53c6 (per the DOAJ listing, which is the most direct source for the DOI)
- **Volume and issue:** Volume 971, issue 1. The DOAJ listing gives article number 83, but the Royal Observatory of Belgium record gives "pp. 17," so the page or article number is inconsistent across sources and should be checked against the journal.
- **Preprint:** arXiv 2405.09693 (an ar5iv HTML version is indexed).

On findings, the authors report that the WSA configurations that best matched PSP observations near the Sun were not the ones that gave better predictions at Earth. They attribute part of this to few fast solar wind streams being recorded by PSP, and they note that the calibration relied on unexpectedly slow velocities.

- (a) Arge et al. 2003 (AIP Conf. Proc. 679, 190, doi:10.1063/1.1618574) and Arge et al. 2004 (JASTP 66, 1295, doi:10.1016/j.jastp.2004.03.018): **coefficients UNVERIFIED**. - (b) McGregor et al. 2011 (JGR 116, A03101, doi:10.1029/2010JA015881): the primary is paywalled, so **coefficients UNVERIFIED**. Zhang et al. 2023 (Front. Astron. Space Sci. 10, 1105797, doi:10.3389/fspas.2023.1105797) is secondary only. It lists the generic form V_min + (V_max−V_min)/(1+f_s)^a1·[1−0.8 exp(−(θ_b/a2)^a3)]^a4. - (d) Reiss et al. 2019 (ApJS 240, 35, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/aaf8b3), Eq. 12: v = v0 + (v1−v0)/(1+f_p)^α·{β − γ exp[−(d/w)^δ]}³. Values: v0=285, v1=910 (so v1−v0 = 625), α=2/9, β=1, γ=0.8, w=2, δ=3. Units of w are not stated. Applied at 5 R☉ and then mapped outward with HUX. No optimized values are given.
  - Note: the paper prints **δ=3**, while your header uses ^2.0.
- (d) Reiss et al. 2020 (ApJ 891, 165, doi:10.3847/1538-4357/ab78a0), eight-coefficient form:
  - Defaults: c1=250, c2=650, c3=0.29, c4=1, c5=0.8, c6=3°, c7=1.75, c8=3.
  - Sensitivity ranking: c4 > c1 > c3 > c2. Only these four are perturbed (±4%, 625 members); the coefficients are re-selected each Carrington rotation from the top 1000 runs. No single fixed optimum is reported.
  - Skill (CR2047–2167, near Earth): RMSE 111.0 → 93.6 km/s and correlation 0.43 → 0.50 for adaptive WSA. Only ACE data are used, not STEREO.
- (e) WSA v4.x/v5.x: **no published coefficients found (UNVERIFIED)**.
  - Mays et al. 2025 (NASA/NOAA MOU report, arXiv:2512.14462) says only that "WSA version 4.5 uses different coefficients in the velocity equation."
  - The CCMC WSA~5.4 and WSA~v.5.2 pages give no equation. They place speed at 5 R☉, or 21.5 R☉ when driving ENLIL. **CCMC retired WSA 5.4 from its Continuous Runs System on 8 Dec 2025.**
  - Your VELEQN header is consistent with the Reiss 2019 form (285, 625, 2/9, 0.8, w=2°, exponent 3), except for δ.

**2. ENLIL inner boundary (21.5 R☉)**
- **a6b1**, from CCMC run Lan_Jian_112717_SH_1 (ENLIL 2.8f, WSA 2.2), metadata at ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/ror/api/run_metadata.php?runnumber=Lan_Jian_112717_SH_1:
  - vfast = 700 and vslow = 200 km/s.
  - vrfast = 25 ("reduction of the maximum flow velocity") and vrslow = 75 ("reduction of the minimum") km/s.
  - bfast = 350 nT, bscl = 4.
  - **dfast = 125 cm⁻³, tfast = 1.5 MK**, xalpha = 0.05.
  - γ = 1.6666667; inner/outer boundary 0.1–1.1 AU.
- For comparison, Mays et al. 2025 (arXiv:2512.14462) Table 3:
  - a3b2: vfast 675, vslow 225, bfast 300, bscl 1, dfast 200, tfast 0.8 MK, xalpha 0, heating off.
  - a8b1: 700 / 200 / 500 / 5 / 200 / 1.5 MK / 0.05, qheat = 100000, nheat = 2.
  - The report says ENLIL versions differ in how vfast/bfast/dfast/tfast scale or clip WSA values. CCMC's default bscl for GONG runs is 4–5.
- Rules, from Odstrcil et al. 2020 (ApJS 246, 73, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/ab77cb):
  - Density is derived from speed, N ∝ 1/V² (constant momentum flux).
  - Temperature is set for thermal-pressure balance at 21.5 R☉.
  - Br comes from WSA times the magnetic scaling factor ("default of four for GONG inputs"); Bφ comes from corotation.
  - γ = 5/3 plus volumetric heating, giving T ∝ 1/r.
  - Reference fast wind at 0.1 au: N = 200 cm⁻³, T = 1 MK, Vr = 700 km/s.
- **g53q5**: γ = 5/3 is verified (metadata). Reading "q5" as qheat = 10⁵ is my inference, **UNVERIFIED**.
- **d4t1x1**: the metadata field is "cld" (with dcld/tcld/xcld). Mays et al. 2015 (Solar Phys 290, 1775; arXiv:1504.04402) and Odstrcil 2020 give the cloud as density 4× mean fast-stream density, temperature equal to fast-stream temperature, and radcav = 0. The meaning of "x1" is **UNVERIFIED**.
- Wold et al. 2018 (JSWSC 8, A17; arXiv:1801.07818): most 2010–2016 real-time runs used ENLIL 2.7 a4b1 with WSA 2.2; earlier runs used 2.6 a3b2.
- Odstrcil 2003 and 2004 were not accessed.

**3. EUHFORIA (Pomoell & Poedts 2018, JSWSC 8, A35, doi:10.1051/swsc/2018020; primary returned 403, values from Hinterreiter et al. 2019 arXiv:1907.07461 and Samara et al. 2024 ApJ 971, 83, doi:10.3847/1538-4357/ad53c6)**
- v = 240 + 675/(1+f)^0.222·[1 − 0.8 exp(−(d/w)^1.25)]³ km/s, with w = 0.02 rad.
- 50 km/s is then subtracted, and speed is limited to **275–625 km/s**. The "675 km/s cap" in your question is **UNVERIFIED**.
- n = n_fsw (v_fsw/v)², with n_fsw = 300 cm⁻³ and v_fsw = 675 km/s.
- T = T_fsw ρ_fsw/ρ, with T_fsw = 0.8 MK, giving constant thermal pressure of 3.3 nPa.
- B_r = sgn(B_corona)·B_fsw·(v/v_fsw), with B_fsw = 300 nT.
- Samara 2024 PSP calibration: V0 = 207, V1 = 725, w = 0.031 rad, β = 0.50 (f measured at 2.5 R☉). It performed worse at Earth than the default.

**4. BRaVDA / HUXt**
- Lang & Owens 2019 (Space Weather 17, 59–83, doi:10.1029/2018SW001857): variational assimilation of **STEREO-A/B in-situ** data, Oct 2010–Oct 2011. Near-Earth speed improved in 12 of 13 Carrington rotations, RMSE −18.4%.
- Lang et al. 2021 (Space Weather 19, e2020SW002698): HUXt with the inner boundary updated at 30 R☉, assimilating STEREO-A, STEREO-B and ACE, Nov 2007–Sep 2014.
  - About a one-third error reduction. The preprint states RMSE −31.4%; the published figure is unconfirmed.
  - Removes the RMSE–latitude bias.
- Turner et al. 2023 (Space Weather 21, e2023SW003457): **near-real-time STEREO** plus ACE/DSCOVR data work about as well as science data. Speed mean absolute error falls about 46%.

**5. Status, Nov–Dec 2025**
- **PUNCH**: launched 11 Mar 2025. "Data are live" at SDAC since 19 May 2025, updated twice daily. L3 at umbra.nascom.nasa.gov/punch/3/ (DOI 10.48322/nnv7-bn21, about 14-day latency).
  - Mosaics versions 0a–0l omit NFI; v0m (Sep 2026) is the first with NFI.
- **STEREO-A**:
  - Beacon data at stereo-ssc.nascom.nasa.gov/data/beacon/; SECCHI L0 at /data/ins_data/secchi/L0/.
  - The SSC secchi_hi/L2 tree was last updated 2014–2015.
  - UKSSDC (ukssdc.ac.uk/solar/stereo) refused the connection, so its holdings are **UNVERIFIED**.
- **LOFAR**: LOFAR1.0 production ended 31 Aug 2024. As of Oct 2025 the 2.0 hardware was in all stations but still being commissioned. **IPS in Nov–Dec 2025 is UNVERIFIED and likely unavailable.**
- **CACTus**: LASCO quicklook catalog covers 2025/11 and 2025/12 (sidc.be/cactus/catalog/LASCO/2_5_0/qkl/2025/11/latestCMEs.html). COR2-A CACTus folders 2025/11 and 2025/12 exist at stereo-ssc.nascom.nasa.gov/data/ins_data/secchi/cactus/secchi-a/2025/.
- **CDAW** (cdaw.gsfc.nasa.gov/CME_list): covers through July 2026, so Nov–Dec 2025 are listed.
- **CCOR-1**: operational since 4 Apr 2025, 15-minute cadence, products at services.swpc.noaa.gov/products/ccor1/.

**6. Coronal-hole checks**
- **CHIMERA** on SolarMonitor: verified for 15 Nov 2025 (7 coronal holes, with area and ⟨B⟩) at solarmonitor.org/chimera.php?date=YYYYMMDD. Reference: Garton et al. 2018, JSWSC 8, A02, doi:10.1051/swsc/2017039.
- **HEK SPoCA** coronal-hole events exist every ~4 h for 14–15 Nov 2025 (lmsal.com/hek/her, event_type=ch).
- **NOAA SWPC Solar Synoptic Map**: daily hand-drawn coronal holes with polarity and confidence. Recent maps at ftp://ftp.swpc.noaa.gov/pub/synoptic_maps/; archive at ngdc.noaa.gov/stp/space-weather/solar-data/solar-imagery/composites/full-sun-drawings/boulder/.
- **CATCH**: a tool you run yourself (catalog paper arXiv:1907.01990, 2010–2019); there is no Nov 2025 product.
- **STEREO-A EUVI synoptic/synchronic maps** at the SSC end in 2015 (carrmaps/a last updated 2023). Nov 2025 maps were **not found**."
